issues.description: The problem statement and class diagram expect a StockIngredient constructor with signature StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template provides only a constructor with signature StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). The solution implements and uses the three-argument constructor (e.g., new StockIngredient(name, price, quantity)), so students following the specification will encounter a constructor mismatch that prevents compiling or implementing SealSaloon as intended.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) to the template (for example, overload the existing constructor and delegate to it, e.g., public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) { this(name, price, quantity, false); }) or change the template constructor to match the three-argument signature. This will align the template with the problem specification and the solution, allowing students to instantiate StockIngredient exactly as described.

issues.description: Constructor signature for StockIngredient differs across artifacts: the problem statement's class diagram (and the solution) specify a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template repository's StockIngredient only provides a four-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean strictValidation). This mismatch will confuse students (and the example Main) when they try to create StockIngredient instances with three arguments and when they follow the class diagram.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a three-argument constructor in the template that matches the problem statement and solution. For example add: public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) { this(name, price, quantity, false); } or replace the four-argument constructor with the three-argument version used in the diagram/solution so students can instantiate StockIngredient(name, price, quantity) as expected.
